method: Adjudicated the 13 disputes of g-west from the drawing only (prims.pkl via a query script q.py and render.py zooms at 0.1-0.25 m grid), then checked the whole part for misses. Per dispute: rendered the spot, listed every WALL/COL/WIN/WALL-GL/HATCH/D-JAMB/TREE/layer-0 item with coordinates, and read the left elevation (2:1, y_plan = 28.2745 - 0.5 x_elev) for the living-room west glazing (bays, inner leaves, slide arrow) and the stair-hall glazing. Also checked the upper floor above the stair-hall east glazing (solid wall) and the ground context east of the part for circulation. Rules applied: the shared definition of 26 Oct; a glazed corridor side wall and a shower screen are glass walls; glazing in a gap of a wall line is a window whatever its height; door vs window for floor-level sliding glazing from what the drawing shows (elevation leaves, terrace, furniture), with eitherKind only where nothing settles it (gym); optional only where window-in-a-gap vs glass wall cannot be settled (living/dining glazing, the fixed glass corner). Ends at the structural faces of the bounding wall ends, on the host wall axis (0.25 m column lines; the 0.1 m wall for GW-06). Accepted openings were kept verbatim (none is contradicted by the drawing). Miss check: a render with a mark at every final opening and glass wall (final_marks.png), a scan of all arcs (all door swings in the part are GW-04, 08, 11, 13, 18 and the rejected shower door), all layer-0 and door-layer items, and the inventory wall-gap list (every gap is an opening here, rejected, or belongs to g-east). Nothing unmarked was found. Totals: 24 entries = 21 scored (8 doors, 8 windows, 5 passages) + 3 optional windows; 4 glass walls; 4 disputes rejected.
